Q: How to change CheckBox.Checked in VB.NET based on "yes"/"no" column A:

I think you are not getting the current row. since your function is not focusing on it. so make the following changes in the method as well as call:

Private Sub usergrid_CellEnter(ByVal sender As Object, ByVal e As System.Windows.Forms.DataGridViewCellEventArgs) Handles usergrid.CellEnter
    cellclick(e)
End Sub
Public Sub cellclick(ByVal e As System.Windows.Forms.DataGridViewCellEventArgs)
    Dim row As DataGridViewRow
    row = Me.usergrid.Rows(e.RowIndex)
    If row.Cells("ACCESS1").Value.ToString = "YES" Then
        CheckBox1.CheckState = CheckState.Checked         
    ElseIf row.Cells("ACCESS1").Value.ToString = "NO" Then
        CheckBox1.CheckState = CheckState.Unchecked          
    End If
 End Sub

Q: Loop to copy and paste one row below the last paste A:

I would say that you could most likely just solve this with a Vlookup Formula autofilled to the target area. But the below code should do it.

Option Explicit
Sub moveDividends()

Dim wsF As Worksheet 'From
Dim wsD As Worksheet 'Destination
Dim i As Long
Dim LastRow As Long

Set wsF = ThisWorkbook.Sheets("Sheet1")
Set wsD = ThisWorkbook.Sheets("Sheet2")

    With wsD
        If Application.WorksheetFunction.CountA(.Cells) <> 0 Then
        LastRow = .Cells.Find(What:="*", _
                  After:=.Range("A1"), _
                  Lookat:=xlPart, _
                  LookIn:=xlFormulas, _
                  SearchOrder:=xlByRows, _
                  SearchDirection:=xlPrevious, _
                  MatchCase:=False).row
        Else
            LastRow = 1
        End If
    End With

    With wsD
        LastRow = LastRow + 1
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "C").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 5).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "D").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 6).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "E").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 7).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "F").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 8).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "G").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 9).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "H").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 10).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "I").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 11).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "J").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 12).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "K").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 13).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "L").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 14).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "M").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 15).Value
            wsD.Cells(LastRow, "N").Value = wsF.Cells(2, 16).Value
    End With
End Sub

Q: How to build a unified C++ cross-platform Windows and Linux (x86_64/aarch64) build system using Python, CMake, and Docker A:

(I would not try to force Docker into this workflow; I especially would not try to force a WINE emulator inside an already-isolated Docker container. One of Docker's core design goals is that a container can't directly access the host's filesystem, and a side effect of the way that's implemented is that it's trivial to bypass all permission checks. So you could in theory

sudo docker run \
  --rm \
  -w "$PWD" \
  -v "$PWD:$PWD" \
  -u $(id -u) \
  registry.example.com/your-build-image \
  c++ -o file.o ... file.cpp

for each source file...but that's a lot of command to run already, and it requires being root [or giving yourself root-equivalent permissions], plus you need to maintain the images with the build tools and all of the library dependencies, and that doesn't capture the requirement to have a full Windows environent available.)

Q: Playwright (Edge) fails after "Switch Edge profile" during login.microsoftonline (Target page has been closed) A:

The issue was resolved by pointing the setup to login.microsoftonline.com/<instance><tenantId>.

I suggest trying to log in manually once and see what these IDs are passed in the URL parameter and just pass them as environment variables.
